title: Recollecting peace
hookLine: do not disturb, airplane mode, the hour after guests leave; the path points at a bigger quiet and names it
tomorrow: bandits demand one of four people. who do you hand over?

cards: Do not disturb. Airplane mode. The hour after the last guest leaves and the dishwasher hums.
Small quiets, chased all week. The Buddhist path points at a bigger one, and names it: nibbana. In one sutta it comes with a picture: a flame blown out by the wind, gone to rest.
Recollecting peace means calling that quiet to mind on purpose, even before anyone has reached it.

teach.b: The Visuddhimagga calls it upasamanussati, the recollection of peace. You call to mind what nibbana is said to be: the fading of passion, the end of thirst, clinging uprooted, craving destroyed, cessation.

teach.h: A LIST OF ENDINGS, HEARD AS PEACE.
teach.b: It sounds like a list of endings, and it is. But the manual hears it as peace: everything that churns, gone still. The Dhammapada puts it in one line: there's no happiness beyond peace.
The manual is honest about one thing.
This subject fully belongs to someone who has tasted that peace; anyone else can still turn toward it. And the week that brought you here was a set of ways to steady the mind for that turn.
Recollecting virtue: glad of my conduct. Generosity: glad of my giving. The gods: the bright ones.
Maranasati: death is certain. The body, known. The breath, again.
Today names what the steadying leans toward.

how: In Theravada practice the recollection of peace is one of the forty meditation subjects; it is taught as a quiet turning of the mind toward nibbana as peace.

o: remembering a calm place you once visited
calling to mind nibbana as deep peace
praying for peace between all nations

games.q: the quiet, named — tap the pairs.
p: a picture of going to rest

s: nibbana is a heaven you go to after you die
the texts describe it as passion fading, thirst ended, craving destroyed: peace.
the manual says only someone who has tasted that peace fully has this subject
anyone else can still turn toward it.

games.q: your friend finishes a giant project and says, 'now i'll finally be at peace.' a week later she's restless again. what does recollecting peace point to?
o: she needs a bigger project to feel done for good.
a peace that isn't a finished task: craving gone still.
peace means never wanting anything, so she's failing.
games.why: the list the manual recalls is about craving and clinging going quiet, not about a task getting done. that's why the next project never quite delivers it.

practice: Find the quietest sound in the room, a hum, a far-off car, the breath itself, and rest your attention there. Let it be enough; when the mind starts churning, let the churning fade the way a sound fades out.

wordCard.voice: Recollecting peace: calling nibbana to mind as peace, the stilling of everything that churns. The week's last subject.

orig.note: Pali: upasama, calming or peace, with anussati, recollection.

carryVoice: Keep this one: peace, the quiet the whole path leans toward. Twenty-eight of forty, and the week is closed.

sources.ref: Visuddhimagga 8 (recollection of peace, upasamanussati, on the qualities of nibbana)
Anguttara Nikaya 4.34 (nibbana as the fading of passion, the removal of thirst, the uprooting of attachment, the destruction of craving, cessation)
Sutta Nipata 5.7, verse 1074 (as a flame blown out by the wind goes to rest)
